verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a complex, multi-step relationship between hedergenin 3-O-beta-D-glucuronopyranoside-6'-O-methyl ester and Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 6. The compound is first identified as a target of Endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 2, which in turn is targeted by a specific metabolite. This metabolite, 1-hydroxy-2-(1-hydroxypropan-2-yl)-8,8-dimethyl-6,7-dihydro-5H-phenanthrene-3,4-dione, is directly linked to Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 6. This implies that the compound may act as a substrate or modulator of the aminopeptidase enzyme, which in turn influences the activity of the phosphodiesterase enzyme. The pathway suggests a potential role for the compound in regulating intracellular signaling through the modulation of these enzymes, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
